solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Alice crumbling up last of layer cake

indicators.note: something crumbling up falls to pieces, so the name Alice is broken and rebuilt in a new order
last of points to the final letter of the word layer

explanation.surface: Alice watches the top tier of a layer cake fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling up' rearranges ALICE into ECLAI; 'last of' takes R from layer.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream, a kind of small cake.

clue.text: I printed anyhow, being fearless

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, haphazard way, so the letters of I printed are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone bravely prints things carelessly, not caring how they turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges the letters of I PRINTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid is a close synonym: bold and undaunted in the face of danger.

clue.text: Source of early training? Piano salesman's reportedly unenthusiastic

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a rep is a sales representative; with the 's it gives a possessive

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for unenthusiastic is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: cool means lukewarm or unenthusiastic

explanation.surface: A piano salesman is said to be lukewarm about something.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'P rep's cool' matches the two-word answer. A British prep school is a private school for younger children.
explanation.definitionFit: A preparatory school educates young children, so it is where early training comes from; the question mark flags the loose wording.

clue.text: In addition, luxurious hotel omitted

indicators.note: omitted tells us a piece is left out of the word before it

parts.note: plush means luxurious or opulent
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A luxury hotel has been left off a list, in addition to others.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition or adverb this word means besides or as well, an extra on top.

clue.text: What we're called in explosive contest?

indicators.note: in places the phrase for what we are called within the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
what we are called is our name

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the name given to us in some explosive competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What we're called' reads as a question but is a phrase to swap for its two-word answer; 'explosive' is a noun here, not an adjective on 'contest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a series of matches in a competition, so a contest.

clue.text: Intelligence needed to secure right legal document

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so one word wraps round the other letter

parts.note: wit means mental sharpness or intelligence

explanation.surface: You need brains to obtain the correct court paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written order issued by a court, a classic legal document.

clue.text: Old article about northern programme

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for old goes round the letter for northern

parts.note: aged means old
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An old piece of writing about the north of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list or programme of items to be dealt with at a meeting.

clue.text: First to scale mountain, most dangerous

indicators.note: First to points to the opening letter of the next word, scale

parts.note: Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: Being the first to climb a peak is extremely perilous.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe can mean serious or dangerous, so the superlative is the most dangerous.

clue.text: Singer, trained at control

indicators.note: trained suggests being shaped or reworked, so the letters of at control are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer has been trained in vocal control.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, or a singer with one.

clue.text: Profligate pinching grand, the scoundrel

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so one word encloses the letter

parts.note: a roué is a debauched, profligate man
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A wastrel who steals a thousand is a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal, a synonym for a scoundrel.

clue.text: A rugby player — very large, incidentally

parts.note: a prop is a forward position in rugby's front row
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very large

explanation.surface: Mentioned in passing: a rugby forward who is enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British label for very large clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used alone as an adverb, means by the way or incidentally.

clue.text: Body of aides always keeping one back

indicators.note: back means the whole construction is read in the reverse direction
keeping means holding inside, so the word for always surrounds the word for one

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: A group of helpers who always keep someone in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' governs the whole assembly, not just 'one': the poetic contraction for always takes the word for one inside it before everything is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Mean to return for a conversation

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word for mean is read backwards

parts.note: par is an average or mean level

explanation.surface: Someone intends to come back for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rap is slang, chiefly American, for talk or a chat, as in having a rap with someone.

clue.text: Join forces with colonel and hold forth about Labour

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party
to orate is to hold forth in a speech

explanation.surface: A politician teams up with an army officer and lectures about the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To collaborate is to work together, pooling efforts towards one aim.

clue.text: Gay old eccentric eager to come up with a fiver in Bow?

definitions.note: in Cockney rhyming slang, a fiver is called by the name of the naked rider of Coventry, rhyming with fiver

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of Gay old are rearranged
in a down clue, to come up means to be read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: avid means eager

explanation.surface: A cheerful old oddball keen to hand over five pounds in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges GAY OLD into LADYGO; 'to come up' reverses AVID into DIVA. Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses the legendary naked rider's name, which rhymes with fiver, for a five-pound note.

clue.text: Award presented to fantastic English playwright

parts.note: an Oscar is the Academy Award for films
wild can mean fantastic or extravagant, as in wild ideas

explanation.surface: A prize is given to a marvellous English dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish writer of The Importance of Being Earnest is a famous playwright, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Drive in Beverly Hills — stick on Wilshire, ultimately heading for Olympic

parts.note: a rod is a stick or pole

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Wilshire
heading for points to the opening letter of Olympic

explanation.surface: Directions for a trip around Los Angeles streets on the way to Olympic Boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilshire and Olympic are real Los Angeles boulevards, here only supplying letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodeo Drive is the famous luxury shopping street in Beverly Hills, California.

clue.text: Don't forget about constituent

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a member is a constituent part of a whole

explanation.surface: A reminder regarding a voter in a constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in mind is the opposite of forgetting it, so the imperative is a synonym.

clue.text: Expected to be paid enough

definitions.meaning: a bill payable now is owing, expected to be settled
as in ... care, meaning adequate or sufficient

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to receive a sufficient wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Owed money is said to be payable now, and due care is sufficient or proper care.

clue.text: Celestial body to arrive by end of August

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of August

explanation.surface: Something in the night sky expected to show up before the close of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body orbiting the sun with a glowing tail, a celestial object.

clue.text: Grow rapidly in Greek character's hot chamber

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet; with the 's it gives MUS
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a room is a chamber

explanation.surface: Something growing fast in a Greek's sauna.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this word means to expand or increase quickly, like fungi springing up overnight.

clue.text: Medical Officer on barge, one doing a second job

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships

explanation.surface: An army doctor aboard a barge who has another job on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlighting is holding an extra job, often secretly, so this person works a second job.

clue.text: Old apartment put on sale, finally, in the recent past

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of sale

explanation.surface: An old apartment has recently gone on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means lately or recently, describing the recent past.

clue.text: Like this parking concession

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A parking allowance granted in this fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is something given to appease or placate, a minor concession.

clue.text: Explosive duke in command

indicators.note: in places the letter for duke inside the word for command

parts.note: power means command or control

explanation.surface: A volatile nobleman is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder, often just called by this shorter name, is an explosive.

clue.text: Duck taken from arcade — charge wife denied

parts.note: a mall is a shopping arcade

indicators.note: denied means refused, so the letter for wife is removed from the word for charge

parts.note: a ward is a charge, a person in someone's care

explanation.surface: A bird snatched from a shopping arcade, its keeper's wife left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' drops W from WARD, leaving ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck with the green-headed drake.

clue.text: Gold artist used to create atmosphere

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter uses gilt to set the mood of a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive feeling or air surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: Argue after small child brings one to squalid part of town

indicators.note: after places the word for argue following the other pieces

parts.note: a kid is a child
to row is to argue or quarrel

explanation.surface: A quarrel with a little one drives someone to a rundown district.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid row is an American term for a run-down urban area of vagrants and cheap lodgings.

clue.text: Only one type of music on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as broadcast, heard rather than seen

parts.note: soul is a genre of African-American music

explanation.surface: The only kind of music played on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole as an adjective means single or one and only.

clue.text: Come in to register

definitions.meaning: to go into a room or place
to record something, such as ... data in a log or signing up for a race

explanation.surface: An invitation to step inside and sign the book.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both going inside and putting a name on a list or record.

clue.text: Loved racing on capital racetrack

indicators.note: racing suggests letters whirling around, so Loved is rearranged

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone adored racing on a track in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racing' looks like part of the scene but is the anagram signal on 'Loved'; 'on' simply joins the capital after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is an arena with a banked track built for cycle racing.
